thread:
Maria G: quick heads-up — ran an nsys capture on canary for the 8k interactive workload, and timeline is full of ~500-900us gaps between GPU kernels. looks like prefetch/kind-of-wakeup stalls, not pure kernel slowdown.
Ajay P: can you paste the nsys command + the short timeline snippet?
Maria G: ran `nsys profile -o /tmp/run1 --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt ./bench --seq-len 8192 --batch 1` and exported the timeline. snippet: `KernelX [compute] 0.62ms -> gap 0.78ms -> KernelY 0.54ms -> gap 0.61ms` repeated across 100s.
Samir: interesting — does this align with the recent batcher handoff change? IIRC 6f1b2c3 changed prefetch alignment and the handoff window.
Maria G: yes, canary includes 6f1b2c3. the old baseline (pre-6f1b2c3) doesn't show the gaps. p95 latency moved from ~78ms -> ~118ms under the same trace.
CI-bot: build 2024.11-canary-6f1b2c3 finished, config: PREFETCH_WINDOW=32 -> 64, BATCHER_HANDOFF=epoch-bound.
Ajay P: please run `nvprof --analysis-metrics`? nvprof sometimes gives kernel launch timestamps that are easier to grep.
Maria G: attached small excerpt from nvprof timeline (converted to csv):
```
Time(ms),Event,Duration(ms)
10.234,KernelX,0.62
10.912,KernelY,0.54
11.472,KernelZ,0.60
12.052,KernelX,0.63
```
and computed deltas: 0.68ms gap, 0.56ms gap, etc.
Zoe: did you try forcing the kernel selector to the old path? maybe the selector picks a different kernel variant that requires different warmup behavior.
Maria G: i forced selector -> variantA (old) and the gaps reduced but not gone. looks like scheduling/warmup interplay with KV cache activation.
Luca: hypothesis: the handoff change introduces alignment that delays async prefetch by up to one handoff window. So compute kernels complete but prefetch scheduled at end of window -> idle time.
Samir: can we bisect to the exact commit? run `git bisect start canary baseline`, then test script that runs nsys and checks mean idle-gap > 400us.
Maria G: started bisect locally. steps: `git bisect start 6f1b2c3 HEAD`, automated test script is `tests/perf/trace_gap_check.sh` (returns 0 if gap > 400us). first bad commit flagged -> 6f1b2c3 itself.
Ajay P: can you paste the diff?
Maria G: diff (excerpt):
```
- if (batch_offset % window != 0) schedule_prefetch(next_window);
+ if (batch_offset % window != 0) schedule_prefetch(aligned_window);
```
small change but moved prefetch scheduling to aligned window boundary.
Luca: that matches the symptom. revert locally and re-run nsys?
Maria G: reverted the two lines and re-ran the same harness. baseline p95 78ms -> canary (6f1b2c3) p95 118ms -> revert p95 80ms. nvprof timeline now shows much smaller gaps (80-150us).
Zoe: nice. can you generate before/after perfetto comparisons and push to the ticket? link them in thread.
Maria G: uploaded two perfetto traces -> https://perfetto.dev/trace/before and /trace/after (private). annotated heatmap shows handoff-aligned prefetch spikes in canary.
Samir: we should add a unit/regression test that captures the max inter-kernel gap for small-batch interactive trajectories. maybe run in CI smoke.
Ajay P: agree. also add a config flag controlling prefetch alignment so we can dogfood new heuristic behind flag.
Maria G: opened PR with revert + flag: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4523. tests added and perf regression check.
CI-bot: PR 4523 passed CI (smoke + perf-check).
Luca: can we keep the improved alignment logic but make it opportunistic? if KV cache already warm, don't delay prefetch. that preserves the original intent without the penalty.
Maria G: good plan. filing follow-up task to re-work prefetch scheduling with KV cache state: TASK-1198.
Zoe: huge win. thanks for bisecting so cleanly. :thumbsup:
Samir: can we retroactively check other canaries that included 6f1b2c3? might have impacted a few customers.
Maria G: yes will run the perf-check across the last 3 weeks of canaries and post a summary in #incidents if anything pops up.
Ajay P: appreciate the thoroughness. saved us from noisy regressions in prod.
Maria G: will follow up with the perf artifacts and the short blamelog in the PR description.
